text:
Emily: quick heads-up — found a regression in KV cache warmup hit-rate on Dedicated after the kernel-selection change yesterday. low-level numbers below. :frowning:

Raj: ugh, numbers? where does this live? :eyes:

Emily: short: pre-patch warmup hit-rate ~82% (prefix cache), post-patch ~57%. p50 token latency for cached responses up ~12ms on average. repro on two clusters (eu-west, us-east).

Sam: hmm. was anything touching key serialization/normalization in that patch?

Emily: nothing intentionally, but the heuristic flips kernel choice for long-context models which changed our byte-order path in the KV writer (internal detail). suspect normalization divergence between warmup writer and runtime lookup path.

Maya: if writer/lookup use slightly different canonicalization (e.g. order of kv entries or base64 flags) that could produce non-matching keys and drop hits — also a privacy vector if tenant id got dropped. can you dump an example pair?

Emily: pasted example below (sanitized):
```
# warmup key (prefix)
model:v2|tenant=sandbox|prompt_sha=ab12cd34|len=128
# runtime lookup key
model:v2|prompt_sha=ab12cd34|len=128
```
notice tenant= missing in runtime lookup for some codepaths.

Raj: wow — that would be a cross-tenant exposure risk if warmup entries are shared. if tenant attr absent we could accidentally hit an entry from another tenant. :exclamation:

Sam: is this an encryption/obfuscation change? we rolled a new encrypted-kv format last week. maybe the de/serial path ignores the metadata block on that kernel path.

Maya: action items I propose: 1) immediate mitigation: disable warmup on affected clusters or force per-tenant key-salting at the lookup layer; 2) audit migration: run scan to find keys without tenant prefix (count + sample); 3) long-term: add unit+perf tests to ensure kernel selection preserves key canonicalization; 4) security alert and rotate any potentially shared cached entries.

Emily: agree. I can flip a feature-flag to disable warmup for the flagged model families in ~15m. also started a quick redis scan job: `redis-cli --scan --pattern "model:v2*" | xargs -n1 redis-cli GET` to count patterns. will post counts.

audit-bot: AUDIT ticket created: AUDIT-4371 — "kv-warmup-keying-mismatch — potential cross-tenant hits". Owner: Maya.

Raj: please also add a short perf-regression test to CI that compares warmup hit-rate before/after kernel selection changes (can be a small synthetic workload). if we catch this earlier we avoid the rollback.

Sam: for rollback plan — if disabling warmup fixes hit-rate, we should revert kernel selection tweak and run interop test. I can prepare a rollback PR. :shipit:

Maya: I'll own the audit and rotation plan, and coordinate with infra to run the scan and a selective purge for keys missing tenant-salt. Emily, ping when the flag is flipped and paste the scan totals.

Emily: flag flipped on eu-west, us-east. initial scan: ~1.2k model:v2 keys, of which ~230 missing tenant prefix. will push full sample to drive. next: create migration script to rename keys with tenant-salt where we can prove ownership, otherwise purge.

Raj: thanks — please post a short incident note in #incidents once we have final counts and mitigation completed. also add a perf regression test to the runtime suite and link the PR.

Maya: noted. logging follow-ups (metrics + alert): add `kv.warmup.hit_rate` per-tenant and a regression alert if drops >10% vs baseline.

Sam: and add a unit test asserting that kernel-selection path does not change key serialization (roundtrip). small test but high value.

Emily: will do. thanks team.
